starting_points.name: Go module plus Cobra generator
starting_points.when: A new command application selects Cobra; use the standard-library flag package for a deliberately smaller CLI without a Cobra scaffold.
steps: Install the project-selected Go toolchain and create an empty project directory. Replace paths and module name with real values.
Initialize the module before Cobra. Set COBRA_CLI_VERSION to a selected published version (including v prefix); ensure the Go install bin directory is on PATH.
Generate the command skeleton, review author/license defaults and add application logic and tests.

commands.purpose: Create a new CLI source directory.

commands.run: go install github.com/spf13/cobra-cli@"${COBRA_CLI_VERSION:?Set the selected Cobra CLI version}"

commands.purpose: Generate main.go and cmd/root.go using Cobra.

notes: Choose the actual project license and author; inspect ~/.cobra.yaml because it can alter output. Add --viper only if Viper is explicitly selected.
If Cobra is not selected, go mod init remains required module initialization; flag and Bubble Tea do not require this Cobra scaffold.

follow_up_generators.name: Cobra subcommand
follow_up_generators.when: When adding commands to the generated Cobra application.

commands.purpose: Generate an example serve command for subsequent implementation.

notes: Replace serve with the intended command name; review generated command registration, help and error/exit behavior.

follow_up_generators.name: GoReleaser configuration
follow_up_generators.when: Only when GoReleaser is selected for this application and no release configuration exists.
notes: Install and record the project-selected GoReleaser release first. Review build entry points, targets, hooks and publishing settings; generation does not authorize a release.

preserve: Preserve go.mod and go.sum when generated by dependency resolution; record the Go version and resolved generator versions.
go mod init creates module metadata, not source files, tests, a service structure or .gitignore. Add project-specific ignores, including OS metadata, without claiming they came from Go.
Keep generator-created files as the baseline; document deliberate changes and do not replace standard defaults with a handwritten approximation.
Preserve Cobra command wiring and help/completion behavior; review generator license output before adopting it.
verification: In the actual project, record generator versions and commands, then compare its initial files with a fresh output from the same versions and options.
After source exists, run gofmt -l ., go test ./..., go vet ./... and go build ./... from the module root; a bare go.mod is not a runnable application.

In a disposable copy, check candidate staging includes source and required manifests but excludes binaries, caches, local credentials and .DS_Store; inspect git add --dry-run -A before changing a real index.
For Cobra, exercise go run . --help and generated command help, then test actual exit codes, stdout/stderr and noninteractive operation.

sources.title: Go modules reference: go mod init

integration_steps: After the selected module/Cobra baseline, resolve dependencies and record tool versions; preserve the Cobra-generated main.go and cmd/root.go command wiring. Add a supported Bubble Tea release only when interactive screens are required.

Implement commands through the chosen command structure with injectable I/O, configuration validation, stable exit codes, cancellation and explicit noninteractive behavior. Keep application logic separate from terminal rendering.
Write command tests covering malformed input, stdin, stdout/stderr, cancellation and safe retries; use isolated temporary paths and test terminal restoration when a TUI is present.

When GoReleaser is selected, follow its configuration generator instructions and review/pin the generated configuration and target matrix. Preserve go.mod/go.sum; document installation, supported targets and rollback. No application setup or publishing has been executed.
